(b) README:39 0.878 for label 0.9 should be 0.872. The served page could not be loaded: the egress proxy refused marisstella.app (connect_rejected).
evidence.fitness: A researcher can rerun and extend it in minutes, and the repository did (research/ambient-third, ambient-multistart build directly on it). As research it is one small step in a 46-slug ambient-* chain rather than a programme (research/CLAUDE.md), on a stylised utility model with every parameter invented, against the 2026-10-21 'run the numbers; don't stylise them' direction. Nearest prior work, none cited: conditional dependence between raters in latent class models of diagnostic tests (Vacek 1985, Biometrics 41; Torrance-Rynard and Walter 1997, Stat Med 16; Qu, Tan and Kutner 1996, Biometrics 52 random-effects latent class with a shared latent 'difficulty'; Albert and Dodd 2004, Biometrics 60, showing different dependence structures fit the same data), and item-difficulty crowdsourcing models (Whitehill et al. 2009, GLAD). That conditional dependence makes DS over-estimate rater accuracy, and that the dependence structure is not identified from few raters, are known results; what is new here is only their size in this toy utility model.
evidence.domain: Against latent-class practice: (a) identifiability is probed by three EM starts, not analysed; with two auditors that share a hardness flag, (a1, a2) and the classifier label are only two conditionally independent views of the class, so Kruskal-type three-view identification (Allman, Matias and Rhodes 2009, Ann Stat 37) does not apply and the classifier matrix is generically not identified either (shown above); (b) the hardness-aware estimator is the generator's own structure started near the truth (disclosed), so 'dsH recovers' is a best case, not a method result; (c) multiple starts without comparing likelihoods; (d) 60 replicates per finite cell with no standard errors reported, so 0.0001-0.0003 differences are uninterpretable (the README says so); (e) no literature on conditional dependence. The simulation design itself (fixing each auditor's marginal accuracy and varying only the dependence) is sound and is what a statistician would do first.

defects.what: README states the classifier matrix is identified and that dsH recovers it, but every start used (README, run.py, test) puts the classifier at its true accuracy 0.7. From start (0.95, 0.4, 0.2, 0.95) the same estimator fits the population joint to 2.7e-13 with the classifier off by 0.0158 and the class prior off by 0.0045; the Jacobian of the full-matrix model has 3 null directions that move prior and C. With two auditors sharing a hardness flag there are only two conditionally independent views, so three-view (Kruskal) identification does not apply. Policy utility was unchanged in the cell checked, so the practical conclusion may survive, but the identification statement is false.

No test touches the utility/policy layer that every headline number comes from: flipping argmax to argmin in the Bayes decision rule leaves all 7 tests green. The plain-DS test asserts only |C_hat - C| > 0.02, so a DS that estimates the classifier from auditor 2's labels also passes.

Prior work on conditional dependence between raters in latent class models (Vacek 1985; Qu, Tan and Kutner 1996; Torrance-Rynard and Walter 1997; Albert and Dodd 2004) and item-difficulty annotator models (GLAD, Whitehill et al. 2009) is not cited; both headline findings (dependence makes DS over-trust raters; the dependence structure is not identified from two raters) are known there, so novelty is limited to magnitudes in a stylised utility model.
Extreme-cell DS auditor accuracy at label 0.9 quoted as 0.878; results.txt gives 0.872 (0.878 is the label-0.7 value).

Every utility parameter, the class mix and the auditor/classifier accuracies are invented round figures (disclosed), contrary to research/CLAUDE.md 'Run the numbers; don't stylise them' (2026-10-21); no sensitivity sweep beyond the five hardness cells.
Engine copied from earlier ambient-* slugs with its dead code (draw_audit, draw_audit2, simulate_utility, regret are never called); pytest and matplotlib used but not declared in pyproject.toml.

verdict: A small, honest, fully reproducible simulation: results.txt reruns byte-identically in under two minutes, every README number traces to it, and an independent loop-based Dawid-Skene EM reproduces all ten auditor-accuracy figures (0.810 to 0.878) while own Bayes code reproduces blind 0.3824 and Bayes 0.3917 / 0.4066. It misses the bar on verification (3 of 5 seeded bugs survive, including argmax -> argmin in the policy rule that produces every headline utility) and on claims: the README says the classifier matrix is identified, but the subject's own estimator, started away from the true classifier accuracy, fits the joint exactly with the classifier 0.016 off, and a Jacobian rank check shows prior and classifier are locally unidentified. As research it is one step in a 46-slug stylised chain whose two findings are known from the latent-class conditional-dependence literature, which it does not cite.
